title: The problem
text: Millions of small shops already sell with a PayPal button. But AI shopping agents can't really use them. They have to guess their way through buttons and forms. ShopBridge fixes that with one script tag.

title: Original shop: 0 tools
text: Here is Lin's Tea Corner, an ordinary little shop with PayPal checkout. Ask Chrome's WebMCP API for tools on this page, and you get zero.

title: One script tag: 7 tools
text: Now the same page with one ShopBridge script tag. It reads the product data the shop already publishes, and registers seven WebMCP tools: search, product details, cart, checkout, order status, and capture.

title: Agent-readiness report (AG Grid)
text: The readiness report loads both pages live and scores them in AG Grid. The original shop scores forty-five. After conversion, one hundred.

title: AI agent orders via WebMCP
text: Now an AI agent. The request: buy two bags of jasmine tea and one oolong. GLM 4.7 Flash planned these calls, and each one runs as a real WebMCP tool inside the live page. We cut the model's thinking time from this recording. The agent searches, fills the cart, and creates a PayPal sandbox order. It never pays by itself. It hands back an approval link.

title: Buyer approves in PayPal sandbox
text: The human buyer opens that link and approves the payment in the PayPal sandbox, using a test account. Everything in this demo is sandbox. No real money moves.

title: capture_order → COMPLETED
text: Back in the shop, the order is now approved, so the capture order tool completes it. Status: completed, with a real sandbox capture ID.

title: Safe by design
text: Under the hood, prices are always recomputed on the server from the shop's own catalog, and the PayPal client refuses any non-sandbox host. We built this from the public PayPal and WebMCP specs, without official Store Sync onboarding. Unlike AutoShop, a permission layer for agents, ShopBridge retrofits shops that already use PayPal.
